item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q026_protein_kinase_like_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe supports a broad, catalytic-domain-level relationship, not wholesale functional interchangeability. In SCOPe 2.08, exemplar domains from a canonical protein kinase, APH(3') aminoglycoside phosphotransferase, and PI3K all fall in class d, Alpha and beta proteins (a+b), fold d.144, Protein kinase-like (PK-like), and the single PK-like superfamily d.144.1; pairwise SCOPe comparison of d1atpe_ from mouse cAMP-dependent protein kinase, d1j7ua_ from Enterococcus faecalis type IIIa 3',5'-aminoglycoside phosphotransferase, and d1e8xa4, residues 726-1092 of pig PI3Kgamma, reports their lowest common node as superfamily d.144.1, which is consistent with probable common ancestry of the catalytic core. The three named activities are separated below that superfamily into different SCOPe families: d.144.1.7, Protein kinases, catalytic subunit, for d1atpe_; d.144.1.6, APH phosphotransferases, for d1j7ua_/d1j7ub_; and d.144.1.4, Phosphoinositide 3-kinase catalytic domain, for d1e8xa4. Thus the safe transfer is the existence of a PK-like ATP-dependent phosphotransferase core and template use for the conserved catalytic domain architecture when an alignment preserves the shared core and catalytic motifs. The unsafe transfer is substrate specificity, protein-substrate docking, lipid versus aminoglycoside versus peptide recognition, activation-loop behavior, regulatory subunits, cellular regulation, or inhibitor selectivity from one family to another merely because the domains share d.144.1. Those narrower claims require external evidence such as statistically significant sequence profiles or HMMs within the target family, a structure or high-confidence model showing the substrate-binding pocket and domain boundaries, conservation of the ATP and catalytic residues in the aligned positions, ligand or mutagenesis data for the residues that contact peptide/aminoglycoside/phosphoinositide substrates, and biochemical assays demonstrating the proposed substrate and regulatory response. PDB 1e8x also illustrates the domain-boundary caveat: only its C-terminal catalytic segment A:726-1092 is classified as d.144.1.4; other regions of the same PI3K chain are separate SCOPe domains in other folds, so a full-chain PI3K template should not be treated as a single PK-like domain.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope.get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope.resolve_scop_identifier: /api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.144","mcp__scope.resolve_scop_identifier: /api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d.144.1","mcp__scope.get_scop_pdb_entry: /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1atp; /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1atp/domains","mcp__scope.get_scop_pdb_entry: /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1j7u; /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1j7u/domains","mcp__scope.get_scop_pdb_entry: /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1e8x; /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1e8x/domains","mcp__scope.compare_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1atpe_; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1atpe_/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1j7ua_; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1j7ua_/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1e8xa4; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1e8xa4/parents"]}]}
